chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurārah, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: concerning

A woman rises during the time of salat (prayer), but she does not perform her Zuhr until the salat time passes her by and the time exits. Should she make up the salat (prayer) that she missed? He said: “If she had been negligent, she should make it up; but if she had been diligently occupied with her ghusl, then she does not make it up.”

And from his father, he said: “A woman from his household would become pure from her hayd, then perform ghusl, until someone might say: the sun has nearly become yellow—so late that if you were to see a person performing ʿAsr at that hour, you would say: he has gone to excess. Yet he would order her to perform the ʿAsr salat (prayer).”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: “There is no contradiction between these reports, because what I rely upon in reconciling them is that when a woman becomes pure after the sun’s decline up to the passing of four qadam from it, then making up both Zuhr and ʿAsr is obligatory upon her together. But if she becomes pure after four qadam have passed, then making up only ʿAsr is obligatory upon her, not anything else; and it is recommended for her to make up Zuhr if her becoming pure occurs up to sunset. In this way, there is no contradiction between the reports.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the obligatory ritual prayer under discussion
key_terms.الْعَصْرَ: the ʿAsr prayer, the afternoon salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَوَانَتْ: she was negligent or delayed without excuse
key_terms.ظُهْرَهَا: her Zuhr prayer, the midday salat (prayer)
key_terms.غُسْلِهَا: her ghusl, the ritual bath required after menstruation
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: making up a missed obligatory act after its time
key_terms.مَغِيبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, the end boundary mentioned for the ruling

ai.seo_question: If a woman becomes pure from menstruation near the end of prayer time, which prayers must she make up?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for a woman who becomes pure from hayd during the time of salat (prayer) and whether she must make up missed prayers. It distinguishes between negligence and being occupied with ghusl, and it also records Shaykh al-Ṭūsī’s reconciliation of the reports regarding when Zuhr and ʿAsr must be made up.
